scope: Frontend static assets served on owned loopback HTTP with schema adapters over a single synthetic dataset. Excludes Go backend latency, filesystem scanning, real project count scaling and physical mobile hardware.
dataset: Three shared projects (one with 60 identical semantic tasks, two empty), fixed descending ID order, 20 rows/page; Needle query returns exactly 20 shared task IDs; shared continuous workflow fixture and 30-section task document; API projection shapes follow actual Go source (compact/default, initial provisional, summary counts-only, content-only)
order: AB for even pair indexes, BA for odd; viewport/theme outer order fixed. One discarded instrument-validation pair per case retained separately.
cache: Fresh browser context per app repetition, HTTP cache disabled through CDP and no-store response headers, Service Workers blocked in both products to prevent worker-mediated cache differences. Browser process reused, no CPU/network throttling. External requests aborted. Local fonts and static asset imports included.

actions.initial: Navigate fresh context to project backlog; readiness 20 rendered task rows with exact expected IDs. CDP counter starts on about:blank immediately before goto, sampled after fixed 1500ms elapsed wall time; rAF begins at document init. Negative deltas invalidate sample.
actions.navigation: From ready backlog click first task and reveal Lifecycle (baseline same visible lifecycle section via anchor; candidate dedicated Lifecycle tab). Ready when workflow timeline exists and has positive width. Same fixed 1500ms includes both interactions and rendering.
actions.search: Return to backlog outside measured window, clear query, input Needle once. Ready when actual request q=Needle has completed and 20 expected IDs rendered. Fixed 1500ms includes each product's natural debounce.
actions.scroll: Ready searched backlog at top, scroll actual available list host 400 CSS pixels in ten 40px steps at 30ms spacing; verify start/end and capacity. Fixed 1500ms. If either UI cannot move exactly 400px, mark pair non-comparable instead of silently clamping.

primary_metrics: CDP Performance TaskDuration delta * 1000 (ms main thread task execution in fixed window)
median requestAnimationFrame timestamp gap (ms, full raw gap list retained)
gate: For every comparable viewport/theme/action/primary metric, compare candidate median to baseline median over eight paired samples. (candidate/baseline-1)*100 >10 fails and requires source correction or honest unresolved failure; no noise waiver or threshold change. Paired per-sample ratios also retained. Readiness beyond fixed window or invalid counters invalidate that sample, and cannot produce PASS.
idle: Separate instrumentation runs (not mixed with primary timing): actual SSE connections/counts, identical heartbeat API requests and precise-coverage function invocation deltas; bounded pending polls and complete/error/route/hidden cleanup; browser page close and owned server cleanup. Synthetic hidden-event emulation explicitly distinguished from physical OS visibility.
limitations: rAF intervals measure browser callback cadence, not compositor/GPU presentation or physical touch/OS gestures
No total CPU, GPU, memory or energy claims
Overview is newly introduced; baseline hub comparison is observation only
Final result requires frozen HEAD and asset hashes plus browser executable hash and candidate binary provenance; docs-only changes require runtime hash equality
cdp_time_domain: Explicit timeTicks: wall duration of renderer main-thread tasks; not process CPU percentage or total device CPU. Same setting for both products.
readiness_instrumentation: Bounded passive DOM MutationObserver over childList/subtree, exact shared row IDs or workflow width; scroll capture event confirms 400px. No rAF-based Playwright readiness polling inside primary windows. Any preparatory waitForFunction runs outside measured windows. Ready epoch is performance.timeOrigin+performance.now; raw observed CDP Timestamp window is retained. This corrects preparation observer overhead without changing metrics, 1500ms target, repetitions or 10% gate.
source_validation: Final run requires explicit A65_PERF_HEAD equal to start HEAD, identical before/after complete static asset hashes for both products and identical Chrome executable hash. HEAD change during capture is accepted only for docs/Markdown-only commits with identical runtime graph; other source changes invalidate the final gate even if numeric groups pass.
validity: Every sample requires positive finite TaskDuration and rAF samples, readiness within fixed window, exact expected IDs/scroll movement, and no pageerror in either result. No zero/unsupported counter or failed screen can produce PASS.
